TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 15, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of Dining Facilities Improvements Project Budget Increase Purpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action item is to seek Board of Trustees approval, under the policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents, of an increase to the project budget for the Dining Facilities Improvements project (Hope Commons) .
The budget previously approved, via the approval of the FY27-FY31 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), is $5.3 million.
URI is now requesting a total project cost of $10.0 million.
Points to Consider: The Hope Commons Dining Project was originally placed out for bid in the spring of 2025, with the project planned to be constructed during the summers of 2025 and 2026.
A single contractor responded with a bid that was $1.2 million above the estimated cost.

URI decided to cancel the project due to the high cost and review the bid package with the intent to re -bid the project in the fall of 2025, a more favorable bidding timeframe for summer construction projects.
During review of the project design, replacement of the roof was added.
The roof , which was installed in 2007 and is in poor condition, will be improved to better facilitate replacement of the roof-top mechanical equipment.
The project bid package review, addition of the roofing system , and escalation results in a project cost increase of $4.7 million for a total project cost of $10.0 million.
The bid package as now structured, along with posting the bid in the fall of 2025, will allow the entire project to be completed in a single summer (2026), which will result in less disruption to Dining Services.
Recommendation: I recommend that the Board of Trustees approve the updated Dining Facilities Improvement project (Hope Commons) budget of $10.0 million, with a construction timeframe during the summer of 2026.
Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees approve the updated Dining Facilities Improvements project budget of $10 million as presented.

FTE Cap - Requested Increase • URI has a general FTE cap (currently 2,292) and a “third party” FTE cap (currently 379) for positions funded through research. Our total FTE cap is currently 2,671. • In FY25, URI exceeded its then overall FTE cap of 2,571. During the 2025 legislative session, URI requested a 25% increase to the cap (+642). URI is thankful for the +100 FTE increase provided by the General Assembly. • URI is requesting a 20% increase in our overall FTE cap in FY27 (+542 FTEs) to reach the FY26 ask amount, and to reflect enrollment growth, increased research funding (R1), and increased State investment in URI (operating and capital). • Since we were already over the cap in FY25, URI is again at risk of exceeding the cap in FY26. 16

URI Staffing vs. Growth: Why More FTEs Are Essential • Growth outpaces staffing: Student enrollment grew 19% from FY06–FY26, while the FTE cap grew only 4%. • Flat staffing during expansion: From FY19–FY24, URI added ~100 students, $30M in annual research, and a new Board of Trustees with expanded responsibilities — yet the FTE cap stayed flat. • Structural inequity: Research-funded positions have a carve-out, but auxiliary positions (housing, dining, 20–25% of FTEs) do not — despite being self- supported by fees. • Competitive disadvantage: URI is well below peer R1 universities in staffing for HR, IT, facilities, research administration, marketing, and legal. This undercuts student support, research competitiveness, and economic impact. 17

URI’s People Power Drives RI2030 18 Education Outcomes: More faculty/advisors → stronger retention, graduation rates. Income Growth: Career services and industry partnerships connect students to high- wage jobs. Workforce Development: Competitive staffing retains RI’s best students and attracts talent. Economic Growth: Each new FTE is a job in Rhode Island, strengthening the state economy.

DISCUSSION ITEMS a.
Review of University Debt Enclosure Vice President Abby Benson provided an update on the University’s debt portfolio, including the types of bonds the University may access and how each is secured.
The University currently has approximately $223M total direct debt outstanding.
Vice President Benson discussed the University’s debt by time, type, and bond series.
She also noted that the maximum payment amount is expected to occur in FY28, with the total debt service falling off subsequently.
She also reviewed the factors used for ratings (by Moody’s) and noted that all three major ratings agencies have mixed views on the higher education sector.
Upon questions from the Committee, Vice President Benson noted that the rating agencies do pay attention to state pension funds and endowment funds in their analysis.

Vice President Benson also noted to the Committee that the University hired a new Director of Treasury to strengthen tax compliance, financial governance and policies, and reporting at URI.
There were no additional questions from the Committee. b.
Comprehensive Campus Plan Update Enclosure Vice President Benson provided an update on the Comprehensive Campus Plan (CCP).
She presented highlights from the slides found in the enclosure.
She noted that the CCP will be brought to the Committee (and the full Board) in September for final approval.
The CCP is being developed by Sasaki.
Vice President Benson discussed the “big ideas” that drive the development of the CCP, mainly: improving campus connectivity, wellness (and an active campus), the distribution of housing, engagement with thriving neighborhoods, integrating environmental stewardship, and bolstering the Bay Campus for a Blue Economy.
She also provided detail on proposed changes to specific areas of the campus, discussed landscape and water management on campus (including the proposed expansion of Ellery Pond), and the enhancement of the North Woods trails to maximize their use.

Within a broader discussion with the Committee, Vice President Benson discussed increased pedestrian and bicycle access to campus, opportunities for growth at the Bay Campus (including increased safe water access for smaller boats), and general possibilities for commercial use of University property at the Bay Campus.
Vice President Benson noted that order of magnitude cost estimates for some proposed elements within the CCP will be included in the final plan.
Concluding the discussion, committee members emphasized the need to prioritize projects based on strategic objectives, return on investment, and funding opportunities.

Global Spectrum L.P., d/b/a Oak View Group, Amendment 2 (Ryan Center/Boss Arena Management) Enclosure Vice President Benson explained that this agenda item is a notification to the Board of the University’s intent to enter into a second and final renewal of the contract with the Oak View Group, which manages the Ryan Center and Boss Arena on the University’s behalf.
She noted that though the total value of the contract is not over $5M, it is a strategic contract.

The terms of the contract remain essentially the same with this renewal, though both parties are tightening certain language, specifically around the safe harbor provision regarding private use, and adjustments to the incentive fee structure.
The amendment should be completed by July 1, 2025.

Vice President Benson noted the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic as well as ongoing deferred maintenance that have affected financial performance.
She noted that the University has created an internal Ryan/Boss Advisory Committee to address these ongoing challenges.
The Committee asked Vice President Benson to provide an update at a future meeting.

URI Board of Trustees Finance and Facilities Committee Meeting June 26, 2025 7 Vice President Benson provided background on a proposed partnership with the RI Department of Environmental Management (RIDEM) relative to the use of the W.
Alton Jones Campus, including the issuance of a request for information (RFI) and the seven responses received.
She noted that URI has been negotiating with RIDEM to operate and manage the campus, including investments in capital infrastructure, dam management, and the creation and implementation of a forest management plan.
The University seeks to be a good steward of the property and open it to the public, while reserving the right to continue to use the campus for research and educational purposes.
She noted that the Whispering Pines Conference Center is not included in the proposed agreement.
The Committee engaged in a fulsome discussion regarding the proposed partnership with RIDEM, debating the best use of the property while considering the current financial burdens, deferred maintenance issues, and potential liability associated with the property.

While some Committee members expressed concerns regarding the lack of revenue within this proposed arrangement, other members expressed concern about not moving forward with what appears to be the most viable solution.
Members also discussed the prioritization of resources overall at the University, noting that the W.
Alton Jones campus needs significant investment to make it usable.
Committee members asked for information on RIDEM’s financial investment in the campus.
The Committee suggested that RIDEM provide a presentation to the Committee in the future to discuss their proposed uses.
Vice Chair Sabitoni called for a motion, and on a motion duly made b y Cortney Nicolato, and seconded by Joseph Formicola, and hearing no discussion, it was VOTED: To recommend approval of an Agreement regarding the use of portions of the W.

Alton Jones Campus at 401 Victory Hwy, West Greenwich, RI by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management as presented on substantially the terms in the enclosed Term Sheet, and that any authorized signatory (as defined in the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents) be authorized to negotiate the terms of any documents relating to such transaction on substantially the terms in the enclosure, with any such changes and additional terms as are deemed necessary or appropriate by the authorized signatory, as presented in the enclosure.
